conditions.name: Common cold
conditions.info: A mild viral infection of the nose and throat. Usually clears up on its own in 7-10 days.
self_care: Rest and drink plenty of fluids
Use saline nasal spray for congestion
Warm fluids can soothe a sore throat

conditions.name: Fever
conditions.info: A raised body temperature is often the body's response to an infection.
self_care: Dress lightly and keep the room cool
Over-the-counter fever reducers may help (follow the label)
see_doctor_if: Fever with a stiff neck, rash, or confusion

conditions.name: Headache
conditions.info: Most headaches are tension-type and not dangerous, though they can be uncomfortable.
self_care: Rest in a quiet, dark room
Drink water - dehydration is a common trigger
Reduce screen time and take breaks
see_doctor_if: Headache with fever and a stiff neck

conditions.name: Cough
conditions.info: A cough helps clear the airways. Most coughs from a cold get better within a couple of weeks.
self_care: Stay hydrated and try warm honey water (not for infants under 1 year)
see_doctor_if: A cough lasting more than 3 weeks
Cough with breathlessness or chest pain

conditions.name: Upset stomach
conditions.info: Short-lived stomach upset is often caused by something you ate or a mild viral infection.
self_care: Sip water often to avoid dehydration
Eat bland foods (rice, toast, bananas) when ready
Rest and avoid rich or spicy foods
see_doctor_if: Signs of dehydration (very dark urine, dizziness)
Severe pain or symptoms lasting more than 2 days

conditions.name: Muscle strain
conditions.info: Minor muscle or joint strains are common after exercise or awkward movements.
self_care: Rest the area and apply ice for the first 24-48 hours
Gentle stretching once the sharp pain eases
Over-the-counter pain relief may help (follow the label)
see_doctor_if: You cannot move or bear weight on the area
Pain that does not improve in a week
